item.title: Yaeyama Islands Guide: Ishigaki, Iriomote & Taketomi
item.description: Japan’s southwesternmost frontier, the Yaeyama Islands are a tropical archipelago of jungle, coral and old Ryukyu charm — closer to Taiwan than to Tokyo. Gateway island Ishigaki dazzles with the emerald Kabira Bay, while neighbouring Iriomote is a wild, mangrove-and-jungle island roamed by the rare Iriomote cat, and tiny Taketomi preserves a postcard village of red-tiled houses and water-buffalo carts. Linked by quick ferries, the Yaeyama are an island-hopper’s dream.

item.title: Okinawa Solo Travel Guide: Island Hopping, Diving & Ryukyuan Culture
item.description: Okinawa is exceptional for solo travellers. The island’s safety, ease of navigation, year-round warmth, and the social atmosphere of dive boats and guesthouses create a natural environment for meeting people and going at your own pace. The real reward for solo visitors is the ability to slow down and access Okinawa’s cultural depth — the Ryukyuan history, the local izakaya scene, and the outer islands where group tour infrastructure barely exists.
